plannerMetadata.canonicalMechanic: Living Yuuzhan Vong weapon with quarterstaff, spear, and whip forms. Changing forms is a swift action. Spear form can be thrown and applies a poison condition-track rider. Whip form has 2-square reach, applies the same poison rider, and a proficient wielder can use it to Pin or Trip without possessing those feats. In any form it can spit venom up to 10 squares as a standard action once per 24 hours.

Pin/Trip feat emulation is exact rule-selector authority and must not be generalized to unrelated grapple abilities.
Yuuzhan Vong Simple Weapon proficiency is an alternate route, not a reclassification of the Amphistaff for other species.

recommendation.fit: High-complexity control weapon for characters who can exploit reach, poison, thrown/ranged options, and Pin/Trip utility. Strongest when the build values flexible mode switching and battlefield control.

identities.canonicalPlayerText: An amphistaff is a serpentine creature genetically engineered by the Yuuzhan Vong to serve as a weapon. It has three weapon forms: quarterstaff, spear, or whip; switching forms is a swift action. In quarterstaff form it has all the qualities of a quarterstaff. In spear form it can be wielded or thrown as a spear; if the target takes damage and the attack roll equals or exceeds its Fortitude Defense, the target moves -1 persistent step on the condition track. In whip form it has reach 2 squares; its tail deals 1d4 piercing damage plus the wielder's Strength modifier and uses the same poison condition-track effect. Instead of dealing whip damage, a proficient wielder can use it to pin or trip as though using the Pin or Trip feat without needing that feat. In any form, the wielder can coax it to spit venom up to 10 squares as a standard action; if the attack hits both Reflex and Fortitude Defense, the target moves -1 persistent step on the condition track. It can spit venom only once every 24 standard hours.

plannerMetadata.canonicalMechanicSummary: Heavy blaster pistol with a swift-action ascension mode that fires a syntherope grappling dart for vertical ascent or downhill zipline movement; blaster mode uses 50 shots, the weapon carries two syntheropes, and its bulk imposes -5 on Stealth checks made to conceal it.

rationale.action_economy: The weapon's combat/utility mode switch consumes a defined combat action.
rationale.exploration: The grappling tether and zipline provide explicit traversal utility outside ordinary attacks.
rationale.mobility: Ascension mode directly transports the wielder vertically or along a zipline.
rationale.movement: The tether moves the wielder at a published 12 squares per round.
rationale.nonlethal: The stun setting gives the weapon a nonlethal attack mode.
rationale.offense_ranged: Blaster mode functions as a heavy blaster pistol and deals ranged weapon damage.
rationale.positioning: The tether changes vertical and horizontal battlefield position in ways an ordinary pistol cannot.
rationale.ranged: Both blaster and ascension modes are ranged-use profiles.
rationale.stun: The certified weapon authority includes a stun setting.
rationale.swift_action: Switching between blaster and ascension modes is explicitly a swift action.

notes: Mode switching costs a swift action.
Blaster profile is Inaccurate and cannot attack at long range.
Ascension mode has a 30-square maximum range.

relativeToStandardPistol.recommendationFit: Strong utility/mobility sidearm for characters who value traversal and positioning and can accept lower ammunition capacity, poor concealability, and no long-range blaster attacks.

identities.canonicalPlayerText: The lightsaber features a handgrip hilt that projects a blade of pure energy. Its blade is generated by an energy cell and focused through crystals within the hilt. A lightsaber requires a special energy cell costing ten times the price of an ordinary energy cell, but it lasts almost indefinitely.

exceptions: Shield Rating reduces lightsaber damage normally.

identities.canonicalPlayerText: A shock whip has reach 2 squares. On a hit, after dealing normal weapon damage, the wielder may make a grab attack as a free action against that target if it is no more than one size category larger. This uses a second attack roll at the wielder's normal attack bonus and does not take the normal -5 grab penalty; if it hits, the target is grabbed. Once per turn as a swift action, the wielder can automatically deal 2d6 energy damage to a target grabbed by the whip without another attack roll. If the wielder has the Trip feat, the whip can knock the target prone instead of making the grab attack. While the whip is grabbing a target, it cannot attack other targets. It requires an energy cell.

identities.canonicalPlayerText: A character wielding a zhaboka takes no penalty to attack rolls when using Rapid Strike. A zhaboka is also a double weapon; both ends can be used in a full-round attack with the normal -10 penalties before reductions from feats or talents.
